args.summary: Latest deploy of checkout-api (v2.3.1) began failing health checks in production. Rolled back all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rollback completed successfully; service is now healthy with error rate 0.002. v2.3.1 requires investigation before any redeploy.
args.title: checkout-api rolled back to v2.3.0 after v2.3.1 deploy failed health checks

trace.final:
All done. Here's a summary of what I did:

**Incident response for checkout-api:**

1. **Reviewed release history** — Found that v2.3.1 (the latest production deploy) was unhealthy, while v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production.

2. **Rolled back all production regions** (us-east, us-west, eu-west) from v2.3.1 to **v2.3.0**. Since v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production, this did not require change-manager approval.

3. **Verified recovery** — checkout-api is now healthy across all regions on v2.3.0, with an error rate of 0.002.

4. **Opened SEV2 incident `INC-0001`** — Titled "checkout-api rolled back to v2.3.0 after v2.3.1 deploy failed health checks," with a summary of the rollback actions and a note that v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until investigated. On-call has been paged.

**Recommendation:** v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the root cause of the health check failures is identified and fixed.
